findings.quote: Its mooring chain must be longer than the depth of the water it lies in.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the passage makes this a necessary truth of every floating aid ('a mooring has to be slack. Chain longer than the depth lets the buoy lift to a sea instead of being pulled under by it', 'thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water'), so a student can call option A textually true of the off-position buoy as well. The case is beatable because it ignores the prompt's delimiter: the statement holds of every buoy on station or off, so it is not what is implied by finding one away from its charted place, whereas the key is ('wind and tide swing the buoy about its sinker ... so the light is somewhere inside that circle rather than on the cross printed on the chart'). Flagged, not killed.

findings.quote: Every partial in the bell is lowered by thinning the band of metal that governs it.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the mechanism is stated verbatim ('Each partial answers to a band of metal at a particular height inside the bell, and thinning that band pulls the partial down'), and a founder who tunes all five tightly does thin all five bands, so option B reads as a true consequence. It is beatable: the sentence is an explicit general fact about tuning, true of Kunert's three-partial practice too, so it is not what is *implied* by the intent to tune all five closely; the key is the consequence unique to that intent ('founders cast heavy ... carrying an allowance of metal ... that exists only to be turned away', reinforced by 'Nothing pulls it back up'). Flagged for adjudication, not killed.

findings.quote: Att han förbigår kommunreformen 1863, trots att den gjorde ägandet till magasinen oklart.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the option collides lexically with the reviewer's own complaint about the alternative explanations — 'Men detta står i förbigående, på en dryg sida, och läsaren får själv väga ihop det' — and the ownership clause is verbatim ('kommunreformen 1863 lämnade oklart vem som egentligen ägde magasinet'), so a strong reader can argue the reviewer does fault Grimlund over 1863. Beatable on two counts: Grimlund is himself the source of the 1863 point ('Han antyder själv två. ... Och kommunreformen 1863 ...'), so 'förbigår' is false, and the prompt asks for the criticism of his förklaring (sparbankerna), which is the key's target ('bokens eget bilagematerial talar delvis emot honom'). Flagged, not killed.

findings.quote: Every partial in the bell is lowered by thinning the band of metal that governs it.
findings.note: ARGUABLE (unchanged option, same case as the pre-repair run): the mechanism is verbatim — 'Each partial answers to a band of metal at a particular height inside the bell, and thinning that band pulls the partial down' — and a founder tuning all five tightly does thin all five bands, so the option reads as true. Beatable because the sentence is an explicit general fact, equally true of Kunert's three-partial practice, hence not what is *implied* by the intent to tune all five closely; the key is the consequence unique to that intent ('That one-way arrow is why founders cast heavy. A bell leaves the mould thicker and sharper than the drawing asks for, carrying an allowance of metal ... that exists only to be turned away'). Flagged for adjudication, not killed.

findings.quote: Every partial in the bell is lowered by thinning the band of metal that governs it.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the claim is stated almost verbatim in the passage ('Each partial answers to a band of metal at a particular height inside the bell, and thinning that band pulls the partial down'), so a strong reader can quote text in support and a complaint would have a hook. It is beaten twice. First, the prompt delimiter is 'a founder who intends to tune all five partials tightly', and B is a general mechanism true of every tuner including Corvenden, who 'tunes the hum, the prime and the nominal closely' by the same thinning; it implies nothing distinctive about the tight tuner. Second, 'every partial in the bell' overreaches the five the trade works with ('The tuners here work with five'; the heard pitch is 'something the ear assembles out of the upper partials'). The key's support is both specific and stronger: 'That one-way arrow is why founders cast heavy. A bell leaves the mould thicker and sharper than the drawing asks for, carrying an allowance of metal - twelve kilos on the Larrowden bell, against a finished weight of two hundred and twenty-eight - that exists only to be turned away', corroborated by 'They would meet it four kilos apart at the pour'. Not DEFENSIBLE; key remains clearly best.

findings.quote: Every partial in the bell is lowered by thinning the band of metal that governs it.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: option B is literally true of the passage, which states the mechanism outright - 'Each partial answers to a band of metal at a particular height inside the bell, and thinning that band pulls the partial down. Nothing pulls it back up.' A reader hunting for the textually supported statement can land on B without strain, and that is the strongest distractor case in this unit. It is nonetheless beatable, because it ignores both delimiters in the prompt: the prompt asks what is IMPLIED about A FOUNDER WHO INTENDS TO TUNE ALL FIVE PARTIALS TIGHTLY, whereas B is an explicitly stated general fact that holds of every bell regardless of how tightly anyone tunes it, so it discriminates nothing about that founder. The key A is uniquely responsive and better supported - 'That one-way arrow is why founders cast heavy. A bell leaves the mould thicker and sharper than the drawing asks for, carrying an allowance of metal - twelve kilos on the Cawden bell, against a finished weight of two hundred and twenty-eight - that exists only to be turned away', reinforced by 'They would meet it four kilos apart at the pour'. Key support is clearly stronger than the distractor case; raised for adjudication, not as a double key.
